newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish 2-yr, 5-yr fixed bond prices seen easing.
newsitem.headline: Polish 2-yr, 5-yr fixed bond prices seen easing.

text.p: Prices of Poland's 16-percent, two-year and 12-percent five-year bonds are expected to ease at Thursday's joint 700 million zloty tender, analysts said.
They said maximum yields may rise 0.1 point to 20.45 percent for the shorter paper from the last tender on December 19 and 0.15 point to 18.35 percent on the longer paper.

They expected the yields to rise due to the substantial jump in market rates over the last two months. The average weekly WIBOR rate for three-month deposits rose to 21.69 percent on January 10 from 19.20 percent on November 8.
Analysts said uncertainty if the National Bank of Poland would raise its nominal interest rates in the near term seemed to play a lesser role.
"The NBP is not likely to undertake such unpopular move (a rate rise) now, when its goal (of) higher market rates has already been met," said Piotr Korcz from Bank Handlowy SA.

Since December, the central bank has been signalling that it might be forced to raise its discount and lombard rates early this year if household credit, which doubled in 1996 from 1995, and company credit continued to boom this year.
Analysts said most of the demand at Thursday's tender, estimated at 500 million zlotys, is likely to be on the higher yielding two-year bonds.
"Two-year paper is more attractive," said Jacek Fila from PZU SA, Polish large insurance company.
Some foreign investors have already started to buy Polish two-year paper on the secondary market.
Dealers estimated foreign purchases of those bonds at some 10 to 20 million zlotys daily over last week, which pressured secondary yields to 20.30 percent from about 20.50 percent.
"There are no good offers on the secondary market anymore, and there is no point in buying them below the potential primary yield ahead of the auction," a dealer at a major Polish bank said.
